recommended_action: Stop infusion immediately. Administer Epinephrine 0.3mg IM. Start high-flow O2.
Administer 15g fast-acting glucose. Recheck BGL in 15 mins. Notify physician.
Administer Naloxone 0.4mg IV. Stimulate patient. Prepare for bag-mask ventilation.
Stop IV fluids. Place patient in high-Fowler's position. Consider Furosemide.
Monitor EKG. Vagal maneuvers. Prepare Adenosine if unstable.
Continue routine monitoring. No acute intervention required.
Administer IV antihypertensives. Monitor BP every 5 mins. Assess for end-organ damage.
Place patient supine with legs elevated. Administer IV fluid bolus. Consider vasopressors.
Administer nebulized bronchodilators. Give IV corticosteroids. Consider Magnesium Sulfate.
Obtain blood cultures. Administer broad-spectrum antibiotics within 1 hr. Start IV fluid resuscitation.
Administer Aspirin 324mg. Give Nitroglycerin sublingual. Obtain 12-lead EKG. Activate Cath Lab.
Start therapeutic anticoagulation. Order CT Angiogram. Consider thrombolytics if unstable.

vital_anomaly: Facial droop, Arm weakness, Slurred speech
recommended_action: Activate Stroke Team. Obtain stat non-contrast CT head. Assess NIHSS. Prepare for tPA if eligible.
Protect airway. Administer IV Lorazepam. Load with antiepileptic drug. Monitor EEG.
Administer antihistamines. Monitor for progression to anaphylaxis. Observe for 1-2 hours.
Administer IV Calcium Gluconate to stabilize myocardium. Give IV Insulin with D50. Consider Kayexalate.
Administer IV Potassium Chloride cautiously. Monitor EKG. Recheck potassium levels.
Stop triggering agents. Administer Dantrolene. Cool patient. Treat hyperkalemia and acidosis.
Discontinue serotonergic agents. Administer Cyproheptadine. Provide supportive care and cooling.

vital_anomaly: Lead-pipe rigidity, High fever, Autonomic instability
recommended_action: Stop antipsychotics. Administer Dantrolene or Bromocriptine. Aggressive cooling and hydration.
Check Digoxin level. Administer DigiFab (Digoxin Immune Fab) if indicated. Monitor EKG continuously.
Check Lithium level. Aggressive IV hydration. Consider hemodialysis for severe toxicity.
Check APAP level at 4 hours. Administer N-acetylcysteine (NAC) based on Rumack-Matthew nomogram.
Provide supportive care. Consider Flumazenil cautiously if no chronic use or seizure history.
Administer Glucagon. Give IV fluids. Consider High-Dose Insulin Euglycemia Therapy (HIET).
Administer IV Calcium. Give IV fluids. Consider High-Dose Insulin Euglycemia Therapy (HIET).
Discontinue all Heparin. Start direct thrombin inhibitor (e.g., Argatroban). Send HIT panel.
Hold Warfarin. Administer Vitamin K. Give Prothrombin Complex Concentrate (PCC) for severe bleeding.
Discontinue nephrotoxic agents. Optimize fluid status. Monitor electrolytes closely.
Start aggressive IV fluid resuscitation. Initiate IV Insulin infusion. Monitor and replace Potassium.
Aggressive IV fluid resuscitation. Start IV Insulin infusion. Correct electrolyte imbalances.
Administer Beta-blockers (Propranolol). Give PTU or Methimazole. Administer Hydrocortisone.
Administer IV Levothyroxine. Provide warming measures. Consider IV Hydrocortisone.
Administer IV Hydrocortisone immediately. Aggressive IV fluid resuscitation. Correct hypoglycemia.
Initiate mechanical ventilation with low tidal volumes. Use high PEEP. Consider prone positioning.

vital_anomaly: Sudden pleuritic pain, Decreased breath sounds
recommended_action: Obtain stat Chest X-ray. Prepare for needle decompression or chest tube insertion if tension suspected.

vital_anomaly: Beck's Triad (Hypotension, JVD, Muffled heart sounds)
recommended_action: Obtain stat Echocardiogram. Prepare for emergent pericardiocentesis. Administer IV fluids.
Strict BP and HR control (Esmolol, Nitroprusside). Obtain stat CT Angiogram. Consult vascular surgery.
Administer IV Lorazepam. Load with Fosphenytoin or Levetiracetam. Prepare for intubation if refractory.
Obtain blood cultures. Start empiric antibiotics immediately. Prepare for Lumbar Puncture.
Identify and treat underlying cause. Administer Lactulose for hepatic encephalopathy. Monitor neuro status.
Administer IV Benzodiazepines (Diazepam, Lorazepam) using symptom-triggered protocol. Correct electrolytes.
Administer IV Thiamine BEFORE glucose. Replace Magnesium and other electrolytes.
Establish 2 large-bore IVs. Type and Cross for blood products. Start IV PPI. Consult GI for endoscopy.

vital_anomaly: Severe epigastric pain radiating to back
recommended_action: Aggressive IV fluid resuscitation (Lactated Ringer's). Keep NPO. Provide IV pain management.
Keep NPO. Insert Nasogastric (NG) tube for decompression. Administer IV fluids. Consult surgery.

vital_anomaly: Pain out of proportion to exam
recommended_action: Obtain stat CT Angiogram abdomen. Start broad-spectrum antibiotics. Consult vascular surgery immediately.
Establish large-bore IVs. Type and Cross for blood. Consult OB/GYN immediately for emergent surgery.
Monitor fetal heart rate continuously. Establish IV access. Prepare for emergent delivery.
Monitor BP closely. Administer IV Labetalol or Hydralazine. Start Magnesium Sulfate for seizure prophylaxis.
Protect airway. Administer IV Magnesium Sulfate. Control BP. Prepare for emergent delivery once stabilized.
Fundal massage. Administer Uterotonics (Oxytocin, Methergine). Establish IV access. Type and Cross.
Provide aggressive IV pain management. Administer IV fluids. Administer supplemental oxygen if hypoxic.

vital_anomaly: Elevated Uric Acid, K+, Phos; Decreased Ca2+
recommended_action: Aggressive IV hydration. Administer Allopurinol or Rasburicase. Monitor and correct electrolytes.
Obtain blood cultures immediately. Start broad-spectrum IV antibiotics (e.g., Cefepime) within 1 hour.
Treat underlying cause (e.g., sepsis). Transfuse Platelets, FFP, or Cryoprecipitate as indicated.
Stop transfusion immediately! Maintain IV access with Normal Saline. Send blood bank workup.
Stop transfusion. Provide supplemental oxygen. Consider mechanical ventilation. Do NOT give diuretics.
Stop or slow transfusion. Place patient upright. Administer IV Diuretics (Furosemide).
Ensure adequate pre- and post-procedure IV hydration. Monitor renal function.

vital_anomaly: Pain, Swelling, Erythema at IV site
recommended_action: Stop infusion immediately. Aspirate residual drug. Apply appropriate thermal compress. Administer antidote if available.
Remove IV catheter. Apply warm compress. Elevate extremity. Monitor for infection.

vital_anomaly: Swelling, Coolness, Pallor at IV site
recommended_action: Stop infusion. Remove IV catheter. Elevate extremity. Apply warm or cold compress depending on fluid.
Place patient in left lateral decubitus and Trendelenburg position. Administer 100% O2. Notify physician.

vital_anomaly: Fever, Chills, Erythema at line site
recommended_action: Obtain blood cultures from line and peripheral site. Remove line if indicated. Start IV antibiotics.
Elevate extremity. Initiate therapeutic anticoagulation. Obtain venous Doppler ultrasound.

vital_anomaly: Severe pain out of proportion, Paresthesia
recommended_action: Remove any constricting dressings/casts. Keep extremity at heart level. Consult Orthopedics for emergent fasciotomy.

vital_anomaly: Dark urine, Muscle pain, Elevated CK
recommended_action: Aggressive IV fluid resuscitation to maintain high urine output. Monitor Potassium and renal function.
Initiate rapid cooling measures (ice packs, evaporative cooling). Administer cool IV fluids. Monitor core temp.
Initiate active external and internal warming (warm blankets, warm IV fluids). Monitor EKG for arrhythmias.
Rapid rewarming in warm water bath (37-39C). Provide pain management. Do NOT rub the affected area.
Administer 100% Oxygen via non-rebreather mask. Consider hyperbaric oxygen therapy for severe cases.
Administer Cyanide Antidote Kit (Hydroxocobalamin or Sodium Nitrite/Sodium Thiosulfate).
Decontaminate patient. Administer Atropine until secretions dry. Administer Pralidoxime (2-PAM).
Administer Activated Charcoal if early. Alkalinize urine with IV Sodium Bicarbonate. Consider hemodialysis.
Administer IV Sodium Bicarbonate for QRS > 100ms. Treat seizures with Benzodiazepines.
Obtain serum iron levels. Administer Deferoxamine if indicated (vin rosé urine). Provide GI decontamination.
Identify and remove source. Administer Chelation therapy (Succimer, EDTA) based on lead levels.
Immobilize extremity at heart level. Do NOT use tourniquets or suction. Administer CroFab antivenom if indicated.
Provide pain management (Opioids). Administer Benzodiazepines for muscle spasms. Consider antivenom for severe cases.
Provide local wound care. Update Tetanus. Monitor for systemic signs (hemolysis).
Treat as Anaphylaxis. Administer IM Epinephrine. Remove stinger by scraping. Start IV fluids.
Administer Epinephrine 0.3mg IM immediately. Start IV fluids. Give Antihistamines and Corticosteroids.
Remove all latex products. Administer Epinephrine 0.3mg IM. Provide supportive care.
Stop contrast immediately. Administer Epinephrine IM. Start aggressive IV fluid resuscitation.
Admit to ICU. Reduce MAP by no more than 25% in first hour using titratable IV antihypertensives.
Place upright. Administer IV Diuretics. Consider BiPAP for respiratory support. Give Vasodilators if BP allows.
Obtain stat Echocardiogram. Start Inotropes. Avoid aggressive fluid boluses. Consider mechanical circulatory support.
Establish 2 large-bore IVs. Administer rapid IV fluid boluses (Lactated Ringer's). Transfuse blood if hemorrhagic.
Administer IV fluid boluses. Start Vasopressors if unresponsive to fluids. Treat underlying cause (e.g., sepsis, anaphylaxis).

vital_anomaly: Hypotension, JVD, Muffled heart sounds/Absent breath sounds
recommended_action: Identify and treat cause immediately (e.g., Needle decompression for tension PTX, Pericardiocentesis for tamponade).
Maintain spinal immobilization. Administer IV fluids cautiously. Start Vasopressors. Treat bradycardia with Atropine.
Place patient supine with legs elevated. Monitor vitals. Usually self-resolving. Provide reassurance.

vital_anomaly: Drop in BP upon standing, Dizziness
recommended_action: Instruct patient to change positions slowly. Administer IV fluids if dehydrated. Review medications.
Control rate with IV Diltiazem or Metoprolol. Consider cardioversion if hemodynamically unstable.
If stable, give IV Amiodarone. If unstable with a pulse, perform synchronized cardioversion. If pulseless, start CPR and defibrillate.
Initiate high-quality CPR immediately. Defibrillate as soon as possible. Administer Epinephrine every 3-5 mins.
Initiate high-quality CPR. Administer Epinephrine every 3-5 mins. Identify and treat reversible causes (Hs and Ts). Do NOT defibrillate.
Initiate high-quality CPR. Administer Epinephrine every 3-5 mins. Aggressively search for and treat reversible causes (Hs and Ts).
Administer IV Atropine. If ineffective, prepare for transcutaneous pacing or start Dopamine/Epinephrine infusion.

vital_anomaly: Dissociated P waves and QRS complexes, Bradycardia
recommended_action: Apply transcutaneous pacing pads. Administer Atropine (may be ineffective). Consult Cardiology for transvenous pacemaker.
Prepare for immediate intubation. Administer IM Epinephrine. Give IV Magnesium Sulfate. Continuous nebulizers.
Administer bronchodilators. Give systemic Corticosteroids. Start empiric antibiotics. Consider BiPAP for hypercapnia.
Administer high-dose IV Nitroglycerin. Apply BiPAP. Administer IV Diuretics. Place patient upright.
Administer nebulized Racemic Epinephrine. Give IM/PO Dexamethasone. Keep child calm. Monitor airway closely.
Do NOT examine throat. Keep patient calm. Prepare for emergent intubation in the OR. Start IV antibiotics.
